newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Sturdy dollar support pegged at 124 yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Sturdy dollar support pegged at 124 yen.

text.p: Chartists identified several layers of support for dollar/yen, but they deemed the 124 level particularly solid for both technical and fundamental reasons.
Ture Johnson, a technical analyst at Bank of America, noted that the dollar had broken out of a triangle pattern about one month ago.
The pullback to the top of that triangle comes in at 124, according to Johnson.
"So, I don't think it'll get below that," he said, referring to the 124-yen threshold.

The dollar had come under pressure in overnight trading partly because of fears of concerted central bank intervention to prop up the yen. It had slid below 125 yen for the first time in more than a month.
At midday, the dollar stood at 125.01/06 yen, barely changed from 125.00/10 at the open. Shortly after midday, the greenback dipped below 125 yen again.
John Moore, a foreign exchange analyst at Technical Data, pegged near term dollar support at 124.50 yen, a level he termed a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of the move from 121.35 to 127.50.
If support at 124.50 yen broke, the dollar could work its way down towards 1.24 but there would likely be buying interest in that area, Moore said.

Moore cited several factors that might spark this dollar buying interest, including higher relative growth expectations for the United States versus Japan and yawning interest rate differentials between the two countries that favor the dollar.
In addition, he noted talk that Japanese institutional investors remain very keen to purchase foreign securities such as U.S. Treasuries.
The dollar also stuck to tight ranges against the German currency, trading at 1.7190/00 marks at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT versus 1.7195/05 at the open.
Bank of America's Johnson said he would not be surprised if the dollar remained in a trading range with a slightly lower bias defined by 1.7120/30 marks to 1.7240/50 over the next few days.
Barring any fundamental news that pressures the dollar, Johnson said he expects the dollar to form a base above 1.71 marks and above 124 yen.
